thread:
lina: Pushed the attn-portability branch with both Triton fused kernels and the CUDA fallback. Can folks run quick sanity across SM80 and SM90 GPUs? I saw a weird regression on short seq lengths in CI.

alex: running now on a test rig (A100 SM80, H100 SM90). quick summary: Triton fused is good for long seqs but on SM90 with CUDA 12.2 the p50 for seq=32 is ~10-15% worse compared to our CUDA kernel.

devin: interesting. did you isolate batching heuristics? our runtime switches batching thresholds by arch. maybe we're ending up in a bad codepath on SM90.

alex: I forced same batching: batcher.max_tokens=2048 and batching disabled for prefix caching. result: gap persists. nvprof shows higher divergent control flow in the Triton op on SM90. Snippet: 
```
# nvtx timeline excerpt (simplified)
triton_fused_attn_kernel  1.8ms
cuda_attention_xy         1.1ms
memcpy H2D                0.2ms
```

lina: good catch. Could be Triton generated code picks different vector widths for SM90. Also we recently bumped CUDA toolchain in CI to 12.2. Maybe codegen changed.

tj: tagging batching/kv folks. @devin can you check KV cache interaction? If the Triton kernel touches cache buffers differently we may be paying extra copy/zeroing.

devin: checked logs — when using Triton fused we see extra touch of the KV buffer on allocation path (zeroing to avoid uninitialized reads). The CUDA kernel assumes pre-zeroed pages and relies on mmap-on-demand. On SM90 images our allocator changed to use cudaMemsetAsync which shows up as a kernel. That explains small but consistent overhead.

alex: so two contributors: divergent control flow inside the kernel and extra memset. If we disable the memset path (unsafe) perf aligns.

lina: For the Triton variant we should: 1) make memset async overlap with compute, 2) adjust kernel launch config to reduce divergence, or 3) fall back to CUDA kernel for seq<=64 on SM90. Thoughts?

devin: I can implement (1) quickly in the allocator: submit memset to stream zero_stream and try to overlap with kv prefetch. But tests needed for correctness in Dedicated config.

tj: also consider batching heuristics: for short seqs small batches are latency-sensitive and suffer higher relative overhead. Maybe our policy should prefer the CUDA kernel for latency SLOs on SM90 until Triton wins. Add a runtime flag: enable_triton_fused_for_latency = false by default on SM90.

lina: agree. Let's do a two-prong plan: (A) hotfix: runtime heuristic prefers CUDA kernel for seq<=64 on SM90/CUDA>=12.2; (B) follow-up: allocator memset overlap + file an optimization ticket for Triton codegen / kernel config.

alex: I pushed a micro-benchmark in bench/attn_sm_portability that runs sequences [16,32,64,128,512], seeds, and reports p50/p95 on both kernels and both arches. bench-bot should have posted results to the thread.

bench-bot: Automated bench run: 1768905500-run-001
- A100 (SM80): CUDA-atten p50 seq32 = 0.95ms, Triton-fused p50 seq32 = 0.88ms (Triton wins)
- H100 (SM90): CUDA-atten p50 seq32 = 0.90ms, Triton-fused p50 seq32 = 1.05ms (Regressed)
- Memset accounted: ~0.12ms on H100 path

devin: thanks bench-bot. I'll start the allocator patch and add tests. Lina, i'll add a feature flag so customers on Dedicated can opt-in.

lina: assign: @devin implement overlap memset + flag. @alex add runtime heuristic in batcher and add tests that assert no perf regression on SM90 for seq<=64. PRs by EOD?

alex: will do. Quick note: also confirm cuBLAS/cuDNN versions — small changes there can change vectorization. I'll pin CUDA 12.1 vs 12.2 in a matrix to reproduce.

tj: I'll update the rollout docs: fallback policy and telemetry to detect when Triton fused is chosen and its perf delta. We should alert if regression > 8% on latency SLO routes. :bell:

lina: perfect. If this is urgent we can gate the next deploy to avoid exposing regressed path. Thanks team.

alex: one more thought — paged attention (our experimental KV paging) interacts with these codepaths. If paging moves pages at runtime, it could amplify memset overhead. Add it to test matrix.

devin: noted. adding paged-attn ON/OFF to bench.

lina: ok closing this thread after PRs merged. Follow-ups: #1234 (allocator overlap), #1235 (runtime heuristic), #1236 (triton kernel config opt).
